findings.title: Accidental gitlink submodule added without .gitmodules
findings.body: This PR adds a gitlink entry at the repository root named `sentry-repo`, pointing at the base commit. No `.gitmodules` entry is added, so `git submodule update --init` will fail with a missing-URL error in CI or normal clone workflows, and the entry is unrelated to the feature. Remove this file from the PR.

findings.title: Tests assign to read-only DRF Request.GET and fail during setup
findings.body: `self.request` is a `rest_framework.request.Request`, whose `GET` attribute is a read-only property. `self.request.GET = QueryDict("")` and the later assignments at lines 79, 83, 87, 97, and 100 raise `AttributeError: can't set attribute`, so the new helper tests never run. Build the query string through `RequestFactory().get("/", data=...)` or set the underlying `_request.GET` instead.

findings.title: Discover eligibility uses a naive substring of request.GET instead of the actual query
findings.body: `_is_error_focused_query` returns True for any raw request query containing `event.type:error`, so it also matches negated or mixed queries such as `!event.type:error` and `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`. It also ignores the actual `query` argument passed to `_get_event_stats`; dashboard split calls with derived `errors_only_query`/`transactions_only_query` are judged against the original request query instead. This can apply `upsampled_count()` to transaction rows where `sample_weight` is absent, or skip upsampling for an error-only derived query, producing incorrect counts.

findings.title: Upsampling check uses the outer dataset instead of scoped_dataset
findings.body: `_get_event_stats` receives the actual dataset as `scoped_dataset`, but the upsampling check passes the closure variable `dataset` from `get()`. In the dashboard split path, `_get_event_stats(discover, errors_only_query, ...)` is called while the outer dataset is a metrics dataset, so the helper sees metrics and never applies upsampling to the error split. If the scoped dataset differs in the other direction, the transform can be applied to the wrong dataset. Pass `scoped_dataset` to the helper.

findings.title: Cache key uses Python hash and can collide across project sets
findings.body: The eligibility cache key is `error_upsampling_eligible:{organization.id}:{hash(tuple(sorted(project_ids)))}`. Different project sets can produce the same Python hash, so a cached allowlist result for one set can be reused for another set in the same organization, causing `upsampled_count()` to run for non-allowlisted projects and inflating counts. Use the serialized sorted project IDs (or a cryptographic digest) as the key instead.

findings.title: Internal upsampled_count function is exposed to user queries
findings.body: The new `upsampled_count` SnQLFunction does not set `private=True`, unlike neighboring internal functions such as `count_if`. User-supplied queries can therefore request `yAxis=upsampled_count()` directly, bypassing the allowlist/dataset/query checks in `is_errors_query_for_error_upsampled_projects` and obtaining sample-weighted counts for arbitrary projects. Mark it private if it is only intended to be emitted internally.

findings.title: Top-events ordering and equations still use unsampled count()
findings.body: Only `timeseries_columns` is transformed to `upsampled_count()`; `orderby=self.get_orderby(request)` and `equations=self.get_equation_list(...)` still use raw `count()`. For topEvents requests, the top-N groups are selected and ranked by unsampled counts while the returned series shows upsampled counts, and equations containing `count()` remain unsampled. Apply the transform to orderby/equations or reject those combinations.

findings.title: Upsampling transform applied even when the discover query uses the metrics layer
findings.body: The endpoint can route a discover query through the metrics layer via `use_metrics_layer` (line 311), but `upsampled_count` was only registered in `DiscoverDataset`. The transform at line 296 is applied based solely on dataset/request and does not check `forceMetricsLayer` or the `organizations:use-metrics-layer` feature, so in that configuration the generated metrics-layer query can reference an unknown `upsampled_count()` function. Gate the transform on the metrics-layer setting or register the function there.
